A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffAlign and retain the same central methods, theoretical results, and USPTO-50k experiments despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original USPTO-50k experiments, alignment comparisons, sampling-step analyses, and guided-generation and inpainting examples.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds graph-copying results, component ablations, mapping-noise tests, and additional retrosynthesis evaluations.

M1.justification: The core discrete diffusion procedure, cross-entropy objective, three alignment mechanisms, sample ranking, and guided-generation algorithm remain unchanged. V2's additional experiments test configurations of these components; the broader graph-translation terminology does not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds synthetic 5-by-5 graph copying as an empirical task and evaluates it with corrupted node mappings (Section 4.1 and Appendix G). V1's identity task was theoretical. USPTO-50k and the ibuprofen case remain; the other USPTO subsets discussed in both appendices are not newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster is retained when matching v1 Table A3 to v2 Table 2. V2 additionally evaluates skip-only and matched-Gaussian-encoding comparison variants in Tables A6 and A8. Moving pretrained methods and RetroBridge into the main comparison table is not a baseline addition.

E3.justification: V2 introduces round-trip coverage and accuracy using Molecular Transformer, trains an uncharged-label model for evaluation without charges or stereochemistry, and adds reduced-budget ablations on 512 test examples. It also specifies separate grid-copying and Poisson mapping-corruption protocols. The principal USPTO-50k training and sampling settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds Gaussian-versus-Laplacian encoding and skip-only ablations, mapping-noise sensitivity, prediction-diversity analysis, and a bond-rearrangement case study. It expands v1's qualitative transition-matrix observations into controlled numerical comparisons. V1's detailed guidance-strength illustration, Figure A8, is removed; sampling-step analysis and the ibuprofen case are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's additional tables and training curves retain point-estimate reporting; statements about differences being insignificant are not accompanied by statistical tests.

E6.justification: The principal DiffAlign results remain unchanged, including 54.7% top-1 and 0.639 MRR for PE+skip. V2 revises Retroformer's reported scores, including top-10 from 76.4 to 82.1, and adds copying, ablation, robustness, diversity, and round-trip results. Its new 56.3% top-1 result uses evaluation without charges or stereochemistry and is not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds a cross-entropy derivation showing recovery of identity data with aligned denoisers (Appendix A.3) and Theorem 5 with a proof for intermediate noise levels in absorbing-state diffusion of node sets without edges (Appendix A.7). The original main theorems remain; the arbitrary inference-mapping argument is relocated rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The central expressivity, alignment, and controllable-generation contributions remain. V2 foregrounds general graph translation and describes the unchanged 54.7% accuracy as SOTA-matching in the abstract, replacing v1's explicit highest-top-1 claim across template-free and template-based methods. Stronger retrosynthesis claims nevertheless remain in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 attributes gains principally to matched identifiers, explains skip-only weakness through limited expressivity, and proposes a diversity-versus-round-trip-accuracy tradeoff. Appendix G qualifies mapping-error tolerance with a failure regime in the toy task. Some new superiority interpretations exceed the evidence: Section 4.2 and Appendix D make blanket claims contradicted by Tables 2 and A5.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code link and implementation details for grid generation, toy-model optimization, and mapping corruption. The main architecture, hardware, training-time, and sampling-time disclosures remain. V1's explicit description of the 28 node-label features is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around graph translation and symmetry breaking, including Smidt et al., Lawrence et al., and Xie and Smidt, beyond v1's predominantly retrosynthesis-focused discussion. Appendix D also characterizes DiffAlign as between template-free and template-based approaches because it uses atom mappings, qualifying v1's template-free positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the main narrative are rewritten around graph translation and symmetry breaking. V2 introduces a Preliminaries section, reorganizes theory and experiments, moves retrosynthesis background into Appendix D, and reverses the ordering of the theory and diffusion-details appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adds a contribution roadmap, graph-copying illustrations, diversity and mapping-noise plots, a reaction example, and five comparison tables. It restructures the main results displays, moves v1 Table A3 and ibuprofen Figure A9 into the main text, removes the guidance-strength Figure A8, and adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: V1 did not isolate alignment from positional-encoding benefits or empirically test its asserted mapping-error tolerance. V2's targeted ablations and noise tests substantially strengthen those central arguments, while the intermediate-noise theorem and evaluation without charges or stereochemistry address additional theoretical and comparison gaps. These gains outweigh the new overstatements relative to Tables 2 and A5 and some lost implementation detail. The improvement rests on stronger support and clearer boundaries, not higher main benchmark accuracy.
